items.title: Variables Are Reference Tags
items.content:
In Python, a variable is not an empty box that holds data. Instead, it is a **name tag** or **reference** pointing to an object created in memory.

When you run `score = 50`, Python creates the integer object `50` in memory, then attaches the label `score` to it.
items.explanation: Think of variables as name tags attached to values in memory. When you call the name tag, Python looks at the value it points to.
